issues.body: entry_wall() returns max(median(duration_by_workflow)), but in general median(max(duration_by_entry)) != max(median(duration_by_workflow)). The fetched workflow runs are marginal observations and are not correlated by merge-group entry, so the implementation cannot derive an entry-wall distribution from them. Missing/skipped workflow runs make the mismatch worse. The report and JSON nevertheless label this value entry_wall_median and the research text says the tool re-derives the entry wall, creating a potentially misleading measurement.
issues.fix_hint: Either correlate workflow runs belonging to the same merge-group entry (for example by head SHA/ref or another verified queue-entry identifier), compute each entry's maximum, then percentile those maxima; or rename this output to an honest value such as maximum_of_lane_medians and explicitly state that it is not the median entry wall. Add an asymmetric fixture where median(max) differs from max(median) so the real invariant is pinned.
issues.title: Entry-wall median is not the median queue-entry wall

issues.body: percentile() uses round(q * (n - 1)); Python round performs ties-to-even. This is not the standard nearest-rank estimator (ceil(q*n)-1), despite the docstring and report rationale calling it nearest-rank. For example, the median of two ordered samples always selects index 0 because round(0.5) is 0, while n=4 also selects index 2 because round(1.5) is 2. The estimator therefore changes its lower/upper selection due to parity rather than a stated percentile convention, which can alter rankings for thin samples.
issues.fix_hint: Implement the documented estimator explicitly (typically max(0, ceil(q * n) - 1), with q bounds validated), or accurately document a deliberate alternative and implement it without banker's-rounding ambiguity. Replace the permissive test accepting either middle value with exact expected values for even sample sizes and boundary quantiles.
issues.title: Percentile implementation is not nearest-rank and has banker's-rounding artifacts

issues.body: fetch_jobs() requests per_page=100 but does not paginate. Matrix-heavy workflow runs can exceed that count, so --jobs may silently omit jobs while presenting the result as a workflow decomposition. This conflicts with the tool's fail-loud posture.
issues.fix_hint: Paginate the jobs endpoint until a short page (with a bounded page cap and explicit failure on cap exhaustion), and add a mocked pagination test or factor pagination into a pure/testable helper.
issues.title: Job listing silently truncates workflows above 100 jobs

verdict.summary: The tool is well structured and its filters/reconciliation are meaningfully tested, but two central outputs are not sound as labelled. In particular, the reported queue-entry median is computed from unrelated per-workflow marginal medians rather than per-entry observations, and the purported nearest-rank percentile uses Python rounding rather than the nearest-rank definition. These can silently mis-rank poles, which is exactly the failure mode the change claims to prevent.
